channel.title: News | GATAS Lab
channel.description: News from the lab: degrees conferred, awards, where people have landed, and where we have been speaking. Summer 2026 Four lab members spend the summer at national labs and Georgia Tech Andersen Wall at AFRL, Joana Bou Barcelo and Liam Kunzendorf at Georgia Tech, and George Rauta at ARL Adelphi. May 2026 Tyler Hanks and Luke Morris receive their PhDs The lab’s first two PhD graduates, both hooded in May 2026.

item.title: Four lab members spend the summer at national labs and Georgia Tech
item.description: Four of the lab spent the summer away, at three institutions. Andersen Wall was at the Air Force Research Laboratory. Andersen’s work in the lab has been on structured decompositions and a category-theoretic approach to resource optimization, which he presented at the Undergraduate Mathematics Research Symposium and to the University Mathematics Society in Gainesville. Joana Bou Barcelo and Liam Kunzendorf were at Georgia Tech. Joana works on heterogeneous multi-agent multi-target tracking — she took that to the INFORMS Optimization Society Conference in Atlanta in March — and Liam works with George Rauta on Decapodes.jl.

item.title: Tyler Hanks and Luke Morris receive their PhDs
item.description: Tyler Hanks and Luke Morris were both hooded in May 2026, the first two PhDs conferred out of the GATAS Lab. Both started in 2021, in CISE. Tyler’s work is on the optimization and control side: compositional convex optimization, and a categorical framework for multistage control problems that became Modeling Model Predictive Control at ACC 2024. His thesis runs through coordination sheaves, which are used to assemble a control problem out of parts while still saying something about the whole.

item.title: A Brazilian category theory hub, from Ben Bumpus's group
item.description: Paulo Vitor Macedo Dias, a student of lab alumnus Benjamin Merlin Bumpus at the University of São Paulo, has built Categorias Brasil, which Ben describes as a repository for all things category theory in Brasil. The site collects events, researchers, research labs, outreach material and research blogs in one place. Its main feature is a roster of category theory researchers, which is kept current and is deliberately broad. It includes pure category theorists and people applying categorical ideas in adjacent fields, students as well as established researchers, and Brasilians working abroad.

item.title: George Rauta presents Decapodes CFD at WCCM–ECCOMAS
item.description: George Rauta presented Low-Mach Compressible Navier–Stokes Using Discrete Exterior Calculus on Rectilinear Grids at WCCM–ECCOMAS in Munich, with James Fairbanks and Liam Kunzendorf as co-authors. The World Congress on Computational Mechanics and the ECCOMAS congress are where the computational mechanics community meets, which makes it a useful audience for the Decapodes work. The argument there is that writing a multiphysics model as a diagram of discrete exterior calculus operators is both cleaner to state and competitive to run.

item.title: Ben Bumpus is a professor at the University of São Paulo
item.description: Benjamin Merlin Bumpus is a professor at the Institute of Mathematics and Statistics (IME) at the University of São Paulo, where he leads the CUÍCA lab — Categorical Understanding in Computation and Algorithms — and is part of the CombΘ research group. He announced it on Merlin’s Notebook in February 2026, having moved the previous semester: “as of today I am a professor at the Institute for Mathematics and Statistics at the Univesity of São Paulo (USP)!” He explains the delay as the distraction of relocating to another continent, and a first Carnaval to recover from.

item.title: Wilmer Leal promoted to research scientist
item.description: Wilmer Leal became a research scientist in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the University of Florida in January 2026, working with the Nonlinear Controls and Robotics group. He came to Florida as a postdoctoral researcher in Computer Science in January 2023, after a PhD in Computer Science at Leipzig University and the Max Planck Institute for Mathematics in the Sciences, and degrees in both mathematics and chemistry from the University of Pamplona. In the GATAS Lab he worked on categorical models of compositionality in chemistry, which asks what it means for chemical structure to compose and what a category-theoretic account of it provides.

item.title: James Fairbanks named an ASEMFL Rising Star
item.description: The Academy of Science, Engineering and Medicine of Florida named James Fairbanks a Rising Star at its 2025 Annual Meeting in November. The Academy draws its membership from universities across the state, including FAMU, FIU, FSU, Palm Beach Atlantic, UCF, UF, Miami and USF. The Rising Star award recognizes early-career researchers among them.

item.title: A minisymposium at SIAM Mathematics of Data Science
item.description: James Fairbanks organized a minisymposium at the SIAM Conference on Mathematics of Data Science (MDS24), held in Atlanta in October 2024. The speakers, left to right above: Tyler Hanks, then a PhD student in the lab and now its first PhD graduate; Evan Patterson of the Topos Institute, whose group and ours maintain the AlgebraicJulia ecosystem together; Henry Adams of UF Mathematics; and James Fairbanks.

item.title: Kris Brown joins the Topos Institute
item.description: Kris Brown joined the Topos Institute as a research scientist in 2022, after his postdoc here. He was in the lab from 2021 to 2022, arriving from a PhD in chemical engineering at Stanford. He is the largest contributor to Catlab.jl and GATlab.jl, the libraries the rest of AlgebraicJulia is built on, and worked on ACSets.jl underneath them. His paper with Evan Patterson, Tyler Hanks and James Fairbanks on computational category-theoretic rewriting won best paper at ICGT 2022.
